sections.heading: Function
paragraphs: KDM8 is an epigenetic/chromatin regulator influencing chromatin state, cell proliferation, DNA damage responses, and microtubule/cytoskeletal organization. It is not an established craniofacial developmental gene. Its promoter/TSS region is found to overlap with DEL SV (chr17:66561968-66562967, size:350 bp, freq:0.006).  The portal’s Dashboard contrast distribution of two cases.  It is a 1 kb DEL SV (chr17:66561968-66562967) overlapping with intron No. 3 of the gene.  [Ketchum et al., 2024].

paragraphs.text: Our cohort analysis discovers the case(s) in rare frequency that KDM8 is disturbed as shown here.

sections.heading: Literature
paragraphs: When KDM8 is compromised, downstream signaling required for neural crest cell differentiation and pharyngeal cartilage formation is impaired, which can lead to craniofacial malformations like cleft lip and palate [Chen et al., 2023, Wang et al., 2024].

paragraphs.text: Being an epigenetic regulator belonging to the JmjC-domain protein family which regulates α-tubulin acetylation and microtubule stability, it can facilitate cytoskeletal remodeling associated with epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition. The pathway view illustrates how this DEL SV is mapped in EMT (i.e., Microtubules → cell polarity/cell migration → EMT-like behaviors).
paragraphs.suffix: to see the co-occurring SVs that are appearing with KDM8 in our curated palatogenesis pathway diagram. It shows the involvement of developmental enhancers via the TET-SNAIL4-BMP axis.
